v.f: Price-to-income = house price / annual household income

deep.x: Rough benchmarks
Portugal's affordability problem
House prices in Portugal more than doubled between 2015 and 2024 while incomes grew much more slowly. Lisbon, Porto and the Algarve are among the least affordable areas relative to local incomes.
Drivers
Policy responses

x: Programmes to increase public and affordable housing
Tax incentives for young buyers
Changes to rules for short-term rentals

deep.x: The OECD and IMF have repeatedly flagged Portugal's house prices as high relative to incomes.

cards.title: Coût total de possession
cards.text: Additionnez intérêts du prêt, taxe foncière IMI, charges de copropriété, assurance et entretien (souvent ~1 % de la valeur par an) avant de comparer avec un loyer.

deep.x: Owning a home costs much more than the mortgage payment. Adding everything up gives a fair comparison with renting.
Typical yearly costs on a €250,000 flat
IMI
Municipal property tax (IMI) is charged annually at 0.3–0.45% of the property's tax value (VPT), which is often lower than market value. Municipalities set the rate.
Maintenance
A common rule of thumb is about 1% of the property's value a year on average, more for older buildings.
Compare fairly
Owning isn't "paying yourself": interest, taxes and upkeep are real costs too.

quiz.q: En début de crédit immobilier, les mensualités servent surtout à…
quiz.explain: Plus tard, surtout du capital.

quiz.q: Que s'est-il passé pour beaucoup de crédits à taux variable en 2022-2023 ?
options: Les mensualités ont augmenté avec la hausse de l'Euribor
quiz.explain: Les taux ont monté vite.

lessons.title: Crypto et monnaie numérique
lessons.summary: Ce que c'est et ce que ce n'est pas.

cards.title: Ce qu'est le Bitcoin
cards.text: Le Bitcoin, lancé en 2009 par le pseudonyme Satoshi Nakamoto, est une monnaie numérique sans banque centrale. Un registre public partagé, la blockchain, enregistre toutes les transactions.

deep.x: Bitcoin is a digital currency that works without a central bank or company. A network of computers maintains a public ledger of all transactions, the blockchain.
Satoshi Nakamoto
Bitcoin's creator used the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto and disappeared from public view around 2011. Their identity remains unknown.
Key features
The pizza
On 22 May 2010, programmer Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoins for two pizzas, the first known real-world purchase. At 2025 prices, those bitcoins would be worth over a billion dollars.
Why it appeared then
The first block contained a newspaper headline about bank bailouts from January 2009, suggesting a response to the financial crisis.
Bitcoin's innovation was solving how strangers can agree on a ledger without trusting a central party.

cards.title: La blockchain
cards.text: Une blockchain est une chaîne de blocs de transactions, chacun relié au précédent par cryptographie. Modifier un ancien bloc obligerait à refaire tout le travail qui suit.

deep.x: A blockchain is a chain of blocks, each containing transactions and a cryptographic fingerprint (hash) of the previous block. Changing any old block breaks every link after it.

steps: Tampering with block 1 breaks the chain

deep.x: Why it's hard to cheat
To change a past transaction, an attacker would need to redo the work for that block and all later blocks, faster than the rest of the network combined.
Hashes
Beyond Bitcoin
Limits

x: Public blockchains are slow and costly compared with databases
Many "blockchain" projects didn't need one
Data on the chain is only as good as what's entered

deep.r: it only proves data hasn't changed since being recorded, not that it was correct

cards.title: Le minage
cards.text: Les « mineurs » de Bitcoin s'affrontent pour résoudre une énigme mathématique ; le gagnant ajoute le bloc suivant et gagne de nouveaux bitcoins. Cette preuve de travail consomme beaucoup d'électricité.

deep.x: Bitcoin miners compete to add the next block by solving a puzzle: finding a number that makes the block's hash meet a target. It takes enormous computing effort; checking a solution is instant.
Proof of work
The work makes attacks expensive: to rewrite history, you'd need more computing power than the rest of the network.
Energy use
Bitcoin mining uses electricity on the scale of a mid-sized country, roughly 100–200 TWh a year by Cambridge University estimates.
Proof of stake
Ethereum switched from proof of work to proof of stake in September 2022, cutting its energy use by over 99.9%.
Difficulty
The network adjusts difficulty about every two weeks so that blocks arrive roughly every ten minutes, however many miners join.
Mining turns electricity into security for the ledger.

cards.title: Offre limitée

items.l: à peu près le dernier miné

cards.text: Il n'existera jamais que 21 millions de bitcoins. La récompense du minage est divisée par deux environ tous les quatre ans : le « halving ».

deep.x: Bitcoin's rules cap total supply at 21 million coins. New coins enter through mining rewards, which halve about every four years.
Halvings
Scarcity argument
Supporters compare Bitcoin to digital gold: scarce, so it can't be inflated away. Critics note scarcity alone doesn't create value; demand does.
Lost coins
Millions of bitcoins are believed lost forever through forgotten passwords and discarded hard drives, making the effective supply smaller.
Satoshi's estimated holdings, around a million bitcoins, have never moved.

cards.title: Volatilité
cards.text: Les prix des cryptos fluctuent violemment. Le Bitcoin a chuté de plus de 70 % à plusieurs reprises. Ce n'est donc pas une bonne réserve de valeur à court terme pour de l'argent dont vous aurez besoin.

deep.x: Crypto prices swing far more than shares or currencies. Bitcoin has fallen by more than 70% from a peak several times.
Why so volatile

items: No cash flows to anchor value

deep.x: What it means

x: Poor for money you need soon
Unsuitable as an emergency fund
Leverage can wipe out positions in hours

deep.x: Recoveries
Bitcoin has repeatedly recovered to new highs after crashes, passing $100,000 for the first time in December 2024. Past recoveries don't guarantee future ones; many other coins never recovered.
Only hold crypto money you could watch fall 80% without needing to sell.

cards.title: Stablecoins
cards.text: Les stablecoins sont des jetons crypto conçus pour suivre une monnaie comme le dollar, généralement adossés à des réserves. Certains se sont effondrés quand leur garantie a failli.

deep.x: Stablecoins are crypto tokens designed to hold a steady value, usually one US dollar. Most are backed by reserves of cash and short-term government bonds.

items: kept stable by code and incentives

deep.x: Uses

items: Savings in dollars in high-inflation countries

deep.x: TerraUSD's collapse
In May 2022, the algorithmic stablecoin TerraUSD lost its dollar peg and collapsed with its sister token Luna, wiping out around $40 billion in value within days.
Even backed coins wobble
USDC briefly fell to about 87 cents in March 2023 when it emerged part of its reserves were held at Silicon Valley Bank.
Regulation
EU MiCA rules require stablecoin issuers to be authorised, hold reserves and allow redemption at par. The US passed its GENIUS Act for stablecoins in 2025.

deep.w: A stablecoin is as safe as a bank deposit
deep.r: it's only as safe as its reserves and issuer, with no deposit guarantee

cards.title: Crypto et criminalité
cards.text: Les cryptos plaisent aux escrocs : fausses plateformes d'investissement, arnaques sentimentales dites « pig butchering » et faux soutiens de célébrités. Les transactions sont difficiles à annuler.

deep.x: Crypto's speed, global reach and irreversibility make it attractive to scammers. Most crypto losses for ordinary people come from fraud, not price falls.
Pig butchering

Scammers build a relationship over weeks via messaging or dating apps, then introduce a "profitable" crypto platform. Victims see fake gains, invest more, and can't withdraw. The name refers to fattening a pig before slaughter.
Fake celebrity ads
Ads using deepfaked or misappropriated images of celebrities and journalists to promote crypto schemes are widespread on social media.
Warning signs

x: Guaranteed or very high returns
Pressure to act quickly
Requests to move conversations to private apps
Withdrawal fees demanded before releasing funds

deep.x: Legitimate investments don't come through strangers in your messages.

cards.title: Pas vos clés, pas vos cryptos
cards.text: Si une plateforme détient vos cryptos, vous comptez sur sa solvabilité et son honnêteté. Quand FTX s'est effondrée en 2022, des clients ont perdu l'accès à des milliards.

deep.x: "Not your keys, not your coins": if an exchange holds your crypto, you depend on its honesty and solvency. If it fails, your coins may be gone.
FTX

In November 2022, FTX, one of the largest exchanges, collapsed after it emerged customer funds had been used by its sister trading firm. Founder Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud in 2023 and sentenced to 25 years.
Earlier failures
Self-custody risks

x: Lost seed phrase means permanent loss
Scams targeting wallet keys
No one to call for help

deep.x: Whoever controls the keys controls the coins.

cards.title: Réglementation
cards.text: Le règlement européen MiCA, applicable à partir de 2024-2025, fixe des règles pour les prestataires de crypto et les stablecoins, notamment sur les agréments et la protection des consommateurs.

deep.x: Crypto regulation is catching up. The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation (MiCA) creates a single rulebook for crypto service providers and stablecoins.
What MiCA requires
Taxes in Portugal
Since 2023, gains on crypto held for less than 365 days are taxed at 28% (or can be added to other income). Gains on crypto held longer are generally exempt.
Travel rule
EU rules require crypto providers to collect information on senders and recipients of transfers, like bank transfers, to fight money laundering.
Regulators

x: Banco de Portugal registers crypto providers for anti-money laundering
CMVM supervises under MiCA

deep.x: Regulation reduces some risks but doesn't make crypto prices less volatile.

cards.title: Si vous vous y essayez
cards.text: Une règle empirique courante : n'investissez que ce que vous pourriez perdre entièrement, utilisez des plateformes régulées, activez l'authentification à deux facteurs et ignorez les rendements « garantis ». Ce n'est pas un conseil.

deep.x: If you decide to buy crypto, a few basic rules reduce the risk of losing everything to scams, hacks or panic. This is general information, not personal advice.
Practical safeguards

items.b: strong unique password and authenticator app
consider hardware wallet for larger sums

deep.x: Behaviour

x: Decide in advance how much and why
Avoid leverage and trading on margin
Don't chase coins after big price jumps
Never share seed phrases or remote access to your device

deep.x: Position sizing
Treat crypto as a speculative extra, never as your safety net.

quiz.q: Quel est le nombre maximal de bitcoins ?
quiz.explain: Inscrit dans le code.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce qu'un stablecoin ?
options: Un jeton conçu pour suivre une monnaie
quiz.explain: Généralement adossé à des réserves.

lessons.title: Finance comportementale
lessons.summary: Pourquoi des gens intelligents font des erreurs d'argent.

cards.title: Biais du présent
cards.text: Nous surévaluons les récompenses immédiates par rapport à plus tard. La plupart des gens préfèrent 100 € aujourd'hui à 110 € la semaine prochaine, mais préfèrent 110 € dans 53 semaines à 100 € dans 52. Le délai est pourtant le même.

deep.x: Present bias is our tendency to give too much weight to rewards now compared with rewards later. It explains why saving, dieting and studying are hard: costs are immediate, benefits distant.
Why it's inconsistent
In both choices, waiting one week earns €10. A perfectly consistent person would choose the same way. Economists call this pattern "hyperbolic discounting".
Where it shows up
Strategies

x: Commitment devices: lock money into savings or pensions
Automatic transfers that happen before you can spend
Make future rewards vivid: name savings pots after goals
Remove instant temptations: delete saved card details

deep.x: Make decisions for your future self in advance, when the present isn't shouting.

cards.title: Comptabilité mentale
cards.text: Nous traitons l'argent dans des « pots » mentaux séparés. Quelqu'un peut garder une épargne à 2 % tout en traînant un solde de carte à 18 %, perdant de l'argent sur l'écart.

deep.x: Mental accounting means treating money as belonging to separate "pots" with different rules. It can lead to choices that cost real money.
The cost

x: Pay 18% on €3,000 of card debt = €540 a year
Earn 2% on €3,000 savings = €60 a year
Net loss: €480 a year

deep.x: Using the savings to clear the card would save €480 a year, then rebuild savings with the money no longer going to interest.
Why people do it

x: Savings feel "untouchable", even for a better use
Fear of having no buffer
Different accounts, different mental labels

deep.x: When pots help
Money is fungible: look at the whole picture, not each pot separately.

cards.title: Aversion aux pertes en investissement
cards.text: Les investisseurs détestent tant les pertes qu'ils gardent trop longtemps des actions perdantes, en espérant revenir à l'équilibre, et vendent trop tôt les gagnantes : c'est l'effet de disposition.

deep.x: Losses feel roughly twice as painful as equal gains feel good. In investing, this leads to the "disposition effect": selling winners too early and holding losers too long.

items: sell quickly to lock in gain

deep.x: The evidence

Studies of brokerage accounts, notably by economist Terrance Odean in 1998, found investors were much more likely to sell shares that had risen than ones that had fallen, and that the losers they kept did worse than the winners they sold.
Why it hurts
Better questions

x: Would I buy this share today at this price?
Is the reason I bought it still valid?
Am I anchored to the price I paid?

items.w: "I'll sell when it gets back to what I paid"
items.r: "The price I paid is irrelevant to what happens next"

deep.x: The market doesn't know or care what you paid.

cards.title: Mimétisme
cards.text: Quand tout le monde achète, il paraît sûr de suivre ; quand tout le monde vend, la panique se propage. Bulles et krachs relèvent en partie du comportement de troupeau.

deep.x: Herding is following what others do, assuming they know something. In markets, it amplifies booms and crashes.
Why we herd

x: Social proof: if everyone's doing it, it feels safe
Fear of missing out (FOMO)
Career risk: fund managers prefer being wrong together to wrong alone
Information cascades: people copy rather than research

deep.x: Examples
Buffett's advice
Warren Buffett famously advises being "fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful".
Social media and trading apps can accelerate herding, as in the 2021 GameStop surge driven by online forums.

cards.title: Excès de confiance et trading
cards.text: Les investisseurs qui négocient le plus souvent gagnent généralement moins, surtout à cause des frais et d'un mauvais timing. Une étude célèbre a montré que les traders les plus actifs sous-performaient de plusieurs points par an.

deep.x: Most people believe they're above-average investors. Overconfidence leads to frequent trading, which typically lowers returns through costs and poor timing.
The study

Economists Brad Barber and Terrance Odean analysed over 66,000 US households' brokerage accounts. Their 2000 paper, "Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth", found the most active fifth of traders earned 11.4% a year, against 17.9% for the market.
Why trading hurts
Gender differences
A follow-up study found men traded 45% more than women and reduced their returns more as a result, consistent with greater overconfidence.
For most investors, doing less is doing better.

cards.title: Biais de récence
cards.text: Nous supposons que les tendances récentes vont durer : après une bonne année, on se rue ; après un krach, on fuit, souvent au pire moment.

deep.x: Recency bias makes us assume recent trends will continue. After strong years, investors pile in; after crashes, they flee, often at exactly the wrong moments.
The behaviour gap
Morningstar's annual "Mind the Gap" studies find that investors' actual returns lag the returns of the funds they own, by about one percentage point a year, because of badly timed buying and selling.
Examples

x: Heavy buying of tech funds in early 2000, just before the crash
Massive selling in March 2020, just before a rapid rebound
Crypto buying near the 2021 peak

deep.x: Countermeasures
Last year's winner is not a forecast.

cards.title: L'effet de dotation
cards.text: Nous accordons plus de valeur aux choses une fois qu'elles nous appartiennent. Des tasses offertes à des étudiants « valaient » environ deux fois plus pour eux que pour ceux à qui on demandait de les acheter.

deep.x: We value things more once we own them. That makes us reluctant to sell or switch, even when we should.

v.unit: median value of a mug, $ (Kahneman, Knetsch, Thaler 1990)

deep.x: The experiment
Students randomly given a university mug asked for more than twice as much to sell it as other students were willing to pay to buy it. Ownership alone changed its value.
Money examples
The status quo
The endowment effect links to status quo bias: we stick with what we have. Companies exploit it with free trials, since cancelling feels like losing something.

items.w: "I'll keep it because it's mine"
items.r: "Would I buy this today at its market price?"

deep.x: Judge what you own as if you were deciding to buy it today.

cards.title: Coups de pouce
cards.text: De petits changements dans la présentation des choix peuvent aider : l'adhésion automatique à un plan de retraite et les plans « épargner plus demain » augmentent l'épargne sans contraindre personne.

deep.x: A nudge changes how choices are presented without restricting them. Well-designed nudges help people act in their own long-term interest.
Automatic enrolment
A classic 2001 study by Brigitte Madrian and Dennis Shea found that automatic enrolment in a US company's pension plan raised participation among new employees from about 37% to 86%.
Save More Tomorrow

items.b: savings rates roughly quadrupled in the first study

deep.x: The concept
Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein popularised nudges in their 2008 book "Nudge". Many governments set up "nudge units" to apply the ideas.
Ethics

x: Nudges should be transparent and easy to opt out of
"Sludge" is the opposite: friction that makes good choices harder, like complicated cancellations

deep.x: Design defaults so the easy choice is the good one.

cards.title: Argent et bonheur
cards.text: Un revenu plus élevé est lié à plus de bonheur, certaines études montrant que les gains se poursuivent aux revenus élevés. Dépenser pour des expériences, pour les autres et pour gagner du temps procure généralement plus de joie.

deep.x: Does money buy happiness? Research says yes, up to a point, and much depends on how you spend it.

items: Higher income linked to life satisfaction

deep.x: The debate

A famous 2010 study by Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton suggested day-to-day emotional wellbeing plateaued around $75,000 a year. Later research by Matthew Killingsworth found it kept rising. A joint 2023 study concluded happiness generally keeps rising with income, except for the least happy people, whose wellbeing plateaus.
How to spend

items.b: paying to avoid chores frees time
planning trips brings joy before them

deep.x: Security matters
Financial worries are a major source of stress. An emergency fund and low debt often do more for wellbeing than extra spending.
In experiments by Elizabeth Dunn and colleagues, people given money to spend on others reported more happiness than those told to spend it on themselves.

cards.title: Automatiser les bons choix
cards.text: Programmez des virements automatiques le jour de la paie vers l'épargne et les placements. On ne dépense pas ce qu'on ne voit pas, et on évite le bras de fer avec sa volonté.

deep.x: Automation makes good financial behaviour the default. You rely on a system, not daily willpower.
What to automate
Why it works

x: No decision fatigue
Money moves before you can spend it
Consistency beats occasional big efforts
Euro-cost averaging smooths market ups and downs

deep.x: Review, don't micromanage
Set it up once, review it once a year, and let it run.

quiz.q: Garder trop longtemps des actions perdantes en espérant revenir à l'équilibre s'appelle…
quiz.explain: Dû à l'aversion aux pertes.

quiz.q: Que gagnent généralement les traders fréquents par rapport aux investisseurs patients ?
quiz.explain: Frais et mauvais timing.

quiz.q: L'adhésion automatique à un plan de retraite est un exemple de…
quiz.explain: Cela marche en changeant l'option par défaut.

cards.title: La tulipomanie
cards.text: Dans la Hollande des années 1630, de rares bulbes de tulipe se seraient vendus au prix d'une maison avant l'effondrement des prix en 1637. Les historiens pensent aujourd'hui que cette mania fut plus modeste que ne le dit la légende.

deep.x: Tulip mania in the Dutch Republic in the 1630s is often called the first speculative bubble. Rare bulbs reportedly changed hands for extraordinary prices before the market collapsed in February 1637.
The legend
Charles Mackay's 1841 book "Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds" told of single bulbs exchanged for houses and of economic ruin across Holland.
The revision

Historian Anne Goldgar's 2007 research found the mania involved a relatively small group of wealthy merchants and craftsmen, and caused little wider economic damage. Many stories of ruin were moralising pamphlets.
Why bulbs?
The prized streaked patterns were later found to be caused by a virus, making them unpredictable and scarce.
Even the most famous bubble story was partly a bubble of exaggeration.

cards.title: La bulle des mers du Sud
cards.text: En 1720, les actions de la Compagnie des mers du Sud britannique ont flambé puis chuté. Isaac Newton y a perdu une fortune et aurait dit qu'il savait calculer la course des astres, mais pas la folie des hommes.

deep.x: In 1720, shares in Britain's South Sea Company, which took over government debt in exchange for trading rights, soared and then collapsed within months.
What happened

x: The company promised profits from trade with South America that never materialised
It encouraged buying with loans and instalments
Many other "bubble companies" floated, including one "for carrying on an undertaking of great advantage, but nobody to know what it is"

deep.x: Newton's loss

Isaac Newton reportedly sold early at a profit, then bought back near the top and lost around £20,000, a fortune at the time. The quote about calculating the motions of heavenly bodies but not the madness of people is attributed to him but not well documented.
Consequences
France's Mississippi Bubble, run by John Law, collapsed the same year.

cards.title: Le krach de 1929
cards.text: La Bourse américaine s'est effondrée en octobre 1929, contribuant à déclencher la Grande Dépression. Les faillites bancaires et les erreurs de politique l'ont aggravée.

deep.x: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 ended a speculative boom and helped trigger the Great Depression, the worst economic downturn of the industrialised world.
The fall
The Dow fell about 89% from peak to trough and didn't regain its 1929 peak until 1954.
Why it became a depression

x: Thousands of US banks failed, wiping out savings
The Federal Reserve let the money supply contract
Tariffs (Smoot-Hawley, 1930) hurt world trade
The gold standard spread deflation internationally

deep.x: Human cost
US unemployment reached about 25% in 1933.
Lessons applied

items.b: now act as lenders of last resort

deep.x: The crash was severe; policy mistakes turned it into a depression.

cards.title: L'hyperinflation
cards.text: Quand les gouvernements impriment de la monnaie pour couvrir leurs dettes, les prix peuvent exploser. En Allemagne en 1923, les prix doublaient tous les quelques jours ; au Zimbabwe en 2008, encore plus vite.

deep.x: Hyperinflation is extremely rapid inflation, often defined as prices rising more than 50% a month. It usually happens when governments print money to pay debts they can't otherwise finance.
Weimar Germany
In November 1923, one US dollar was worth about 4.2 trillion marks. Workers were paid twice a day and rushed to spend wages before prices rose again. Banknotes were used as wallpaper and kindling.
Hungary 1946
The worst recorded hyperinflation: at its peak, prices doubled roughly every 15 hours. The pengő was replaced by the forint.
How it ends
Zimbabwe
Hyperinflation's memory shaped Germany's strong preference for price stability, influencing the design of the ECB.

cards.title: Bretton Woods
cards.text: En 1944, les grandes économies ont arrimé leurs monnaies au dollar, et le dollar à l'or. En 1971, les États-Unis ont mis fin à la convertibilité en or, ouvrant l'ère des monnaies flottantes actuelles.

deep.x: In July 1944, delegates from 44 Allied countries met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, to design the post-war monetary system.
How it worked

steps: Dollar convertible to gold at $35 an ounce

deep.x: Why it ended
On 15 August 1971, President Nixon suspended convertibility: the "Nixon shock".

x: US spending on the Vietnam War and social programmes
Dollars abroad far exceeded US gold reserves
Other countries began converting dollars into gold

deep.x: Legacy
Bretton Woods built institutions that still shape global finance.

cards.title: La bulle internet
cards.text: À la fin des années 1990, des entreprises internet sans bénéfices ont flambé. Le Nasdaq a perdu près de 80 % de 2000 à 2002. Quelques survivantes sont devenues des géantes.

deep.x: In the late 1990s, enthusiasm for the internet drove technology shares to extreme valuations, often for companies with little revenue and no profit.
The boom

x: New investors buying shares online
Companies valued on "eyeballs" and growth, not profits
Huge IPOs on their first day of trading

deep.x: The crash
The Nasdaq fell about 78% from its March 2000 peak to October 2002 and didn't regain the peak until 2015.
Survivors and failures
Amazon's share price fell more than 90% during the crash before becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.
A real technological revolution can still come with a financial bubble.

cards.title: La crise de 2008
cards.text: Des prêts immobiliers américains risqués ont été regroupés en titres complexes. Quand les prix de l'immobilier ont chuté, les pertes se sont propagées dans le monde entier. Lehman Brothers a fait faillite en septembre 2008.

deep.x: The global financial crisis began in US housing and spread through the financial system worldwide, causing the deepest recession since the 1930s.
Key events
Why it spread

x: Mortgages were repackaged into complex securities sold worldwide
Credit ratings overstated their safety
Banks were highly leveraged and dependent on short-term funding
Nobody knew who held the losses, so banks stopped trusting each other

deep.x: Aftermath
Lehman Brothers' bankruptcy, with over $600 billion in assets, remains the largest in US history.

cards.title: Le plan de sauvetage du Portugal
cards.text: En 2011, pendant la crise de la dette de la zone euro, le Portugal a reçu un plan de sauvetage de 78 milliards d'euros de l'UE et du FMI, assorti de dures conditions d'austérité. Il est sorti du programme en 2014.

deep.x: During the euro debt crisis, Portugal lost access to affordable market borrowing and requested international assistance in April 2011.
The troika

The €78 billion came from the EU's rescue funds (EFSM and EFSF) and the IMF, about two-thirds European and one-third IMF. Conditions were monitored by the "troika": the European Commission, the ECB and the IMF.
Conditions
Costs
Recovery
Portugal exited the programme in 2014 without a precautionary credit line. Growth, tourism and exports recovered, and public debt fell from around 130% of GDP in the mid-2010s to under 100% by 2024.
The bailout years shaped a generation of Portuguese and a cautious approach to public finances.

cards.title: L'euro
cards.text: L'euro a été lancé en 1999 pour les banques et en 2002 sous forme de billets et de pièces. Le Portugal a converti ses escudos à 200 482 escudos pour un euro.

deep.x: The euro launched on 1 January 1999 as an accounting currency for 11 countries, including Portugal. Notes and coins followed on 1 January 2002.
Benefits

x: No exchange costs or currency risk within the euro area
Easy price comparison across countries
Lower interest rates for countries like Portugal

deep.x: Challenges

items: Germany and Portugal may need different rates

deep.x: Without their own currencies, countries can't devalue to regain competitiveness, which made the debt crisis harder.
Portuguese coins
Each country designs the national side of its coins. Portugal's feature royal seals and the castles and shields of the national arms.
Many Portuguese still mentally convert large prices into "contos" (1,000 escudos) decades after the switch.

cards.title: Leçons des crises
cards.text: Les crises suivent des schémas communs : crédit bon marché, hausse des prix, récits du type « cette fois, c'est différent », puis brusque retournement. La diversification et l'humilité protègent.

deep.x: Financial crises differ in details but share recurring patterns. Recognising them helps protect your money.
Common ingredients
"This time is different"
Economists Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff's 2009 book of that title documented eight centuries of financial crises and found the same belief before almost every one.
Personal protection

x: Diversify across assets and countries
Avoid heavy borrowing to invest
Keep an emergency fund
Be sceptical when everyone's sure prices can only rise
Hold investments you understand

deep.x: Humility and diversification have survived every crisis.

quiz.q: À combien d'escudos équivalait un euro ?
quiz.explain: Fixé lors du passage à l'euro.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce qui a déclenché la crise financière de 2008 ?
options: Des prêts immobiliers risqués regroupés en titres
quiz.explain: Les prix de l'immobilier ont chuté.

lessons.title: Comment les entreprises gagnent de l'argent

cards.title: Chiffre d'affaires, coûts, profit
cards.text: Le chiffre d'affaires est l'argent qui entre grâce aux ventes. Retirez les coûts et vous obtenez le profit. Une entreprise peut avoir un énorme chiffre d'affaires et perdre quand même de l'argent.

deep.x: Every business comes down to this: money in (revenue) minus money out (costs) equals profit. Big revenue doesn't guarantee profit.
Layers of profit

items: Net profit: after interest and tax

deep.x: Big but unprofitable

Many fast-growing companies have large revenues but lose money for years while investing in growth. Uber, for example, didn't post a full-year operating profit until 2023, 14 years after it was founded.
Profit vs cash

x: Profit is an accounting measure
Cash is what's in the bank
They can differ hugely due to timing

deep.x: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, cash is reality, as the saying goes.

cards.title: Marge brute et marge nette
cards.text: La marge brute est ce qui reste après le coût direct des marchandises. La marge nette est ce qui reste après tout, y compris salaires, loyer, intérêts et impôts.

deep.x: Margins show what share of each euro of sales a business keeps. Gross margin covers direct costs; net margin covers everything.
Typical margins
Example: a café
What margins reveal

x: Low-margin businesses need high volume
High-margin businesses attract competitors
Falling margins can signal price pressure or rising costs

deep.x: A business with thin margins has little room for mistakes.

cards.title: Coûts fixes et variables
cards.text: Les coûts fixes, comme le loyer, restent les mêmes quoi que vous vendiez ; les coûts variables, comme les ingrédients, augmentent à chaque vente. Vendre plus répartit les coûts fixes.

deep.x: Costs behave differently as sales change. Fixed costs stay the same whatever you sell; variable costs rise with each unit.
Operating leverage
A business with high fixed costs and low variable costs, like a software company or airline, sees profits swing sharply with sales: great when sales grow, painful when they fall.
Example
Semi-variable costs

x: Energy: partly fixed, partly usage
Staff: fixed contracts plus overtime

deep.x: Every sale above break-even goes mostly to profit when fixed costs are high.

cards.title: Seuil de rentabilité
cards.text: Le seuil de rentabilité est le point où le chiffre d'affaires couvre tous les coûts. Un café avec 6 000 € de coûts fixes mensuels et 2 € de profit par café doit en vendre 3 000 par mois.

deep.x: The break-even point is where total revenue equals total costs. Below it, you lose money; above it, you make a profit.

v.f: Break-even units = fixed costs / contribution per unit

deep.x: The café example

x: Fixed costs €6,000 a month
÷ €2 contribution per coffee
= 3,000 coffees a month, about 100 a day

deep.x: Reducing break-even
Safety margin
The margin of safety is how far sales can fall before you hit break-even. A café selling 4,000 coffees has a margin of 1,000 coffees, or 25%.
Know your break-even before you open the doors.

cards.title: Flux de trésorerie
cards.text: Le profit n'est pas de la trésorerie. Une entreprise peut être rentable sur le papier mais manquer de liquidités si les clients paient en retard. Beaucoup de petites entreprises échouent pour cette raison.

deep.x: Profit isn't cash. A business can show profits on paper but run out of money if customers pay late, stock piles up or loans fall due.
Working capital

items.b: time between paying and getting paid

deep.x: Late payments

Late payment is a major problem for small firms in southern Europe. The EU's Late Payment Directive sets 60-day limits for most business-to-business payments and 30 days for public authorities, but enforcement varies.
Managing cash

x: Invoice promptly and chase overdue payments
Negotiate supplier terms
Keep a cash buffer
Forecast cash weekly

deep.x: Businesses don't fail from lack of profit; they fail from lack of cash.

cards.title: Modèles économiques
cards.text: Les entreprises gagnent de l'argent de différentes façons : vente de produits, abonnements, publicité, commissions ou licences.

deep.x: A business model describes how a company creates value and gets paid for it. The same product can be sold in very different ways.

items.b: others pay to use your IP

deep.x: Freemium
Free basic service, paid premium features. Works when a small share of paying users covers costs for everyone.
Subscriptions
Platforms
Platforms like app stores or ride-hailing apps connect two groups (buyers and sellers) and take a cut. They benefit from network effects.
Gillette's "razor and blades" model, selling the handle cheaply and profiting from replacement blades, is copied by printers and ink cartridges.

cards.title: Économies d'échelle
cards.text: Les grandes entreprises peuvent produire chaque unité à moindre coût : achats en gros, machines spécialisées et répartition des coûts fixes.

deep.x: Larger producers can make each unit more cheaply. Fixed costs are spread over more units, and size brings purchasing power and specialisation.
Sources
Diseconomies of scale

x: Bureaucracy and slow decisions
Coordination problems
Loss of motivation and accountability

deep.x: Examples
Supermarket chains negotiate lower prices from suppliers; chip factories costing tens of billions of euros only make sense at enormous volumes.
Scale lowers costs, up to the point where complexity starts raising them.

cards.title: Avantages concurrentiels durables
cards.text: Warren Buffett cherche des « douves » (moats) : des avantages qui protègent les profits, comme les marques, les effets de réseau, les brevets ou les coûts de changement.

deep.x: Warren Buffett popularised the idea of an economic "moat": a durable advantage that protects a company's profits from competitors, like a moat around a castle.
Examples

items.b: people pay more for a trusted name
a platform is more valuable with more users
changing bank or software is a hassle
scale or location others can't match

deep.x: Moats erode

x: Technology shifts: digital cameras and Kodak
Regulation changes
New business models

deep.x: Why investors care
High profits attract competitors. Only companies with moats can sustain high returns for long.
A great business isn't just profitable; it's hard to copy.

cards.title: Valorisation
cards.text: La valeur de marché d'une entreprise est le cours de l'action multiplié par le nombre d'actions. Le ratio cours/bénéfice compare le cours au bénéfice par action.

deep.x: Investors estimate what a company is worth to decide whether its shares are cheap or expensive. Several simple measures help.

v.f: Market cap = share price × number of shares

deep.x: Price-to-earnings

v.f: P/E = share price / earnings per share

deep.x: A P/E of 20 means investors pay €20 for each €1 of yearly profit.
Typical P/E ranges
Other measures
High vs low P/E

x: High P/E: investors expect fast growth, or the shares are overpriced
Low P/E: slow growth expected, or the shares are underpriced

deep.x: A company's value is the cash it will generate in the future, discounted to today.

cards.title: Un stand de limonade
cards.text: Gobelets et citrons coûtent 0,40 € par verre ; vous vendez à 1,50 €. Votre stand coûte 33 € par jour. Vous atteignez l'équilibre à 30 verres ; le 31e est du profit.

deep.x: A simple example brings all the concepts together: costs, margins and break-even.
The numbers
Break-even

x: €33 fixed costs
÷ €1.10 per glass
= 30 glasses

deep.x: A good day

x: 45 glasses × €1.10 = €49.50 contribution
− €33 fixed costs
= €16.50 profit

deep.x: Improving the stand

x: Raise the price to €2: break-even falls to 21 glasses

lessons.title: Assurance et risque
lessons.summary: Payer un peu pour éviter un désastre.

cards.title: Mutualiser le risque
cards.text: L'assurance regroupe les petits versements de nombreuses personnes pour couvrir les quelques-unes qui subissent de grosses pertes. Chacun paie une prime prévisible plutôt que de risquer la ruine.

deep.x: Insurance works by pooling: many people pay predictable premiums so the few who suffer big losses can be compensated. Each person swaps an uncertain, possibly ruinous loss for a known cost.
The law of large numbers
With many policyholders, the total number of claims becomes predictable, even though each individual's fate isn't.
History

events.l: Great Fire of London spurs fire insurance

deep.x: Why it costs more than expected losses
You pay a bit more than your expected loss to avoid a loss you couldn't survive.

cards.title: Assurer le gros
cards.text: L'assurance est surtout utile pour les pertes que vous ne pourriez pas absorber : votre logement, la responsabilité civile, la santé, le revenu. Pour les petites pertes, s'auto-assurer coûte souvent moins cher.

deep.x: Insurance is most valuable for losses you couldn't absorb from savings. For small losses, paying yourself is often cheaper over time.
Why small insurance is poor value
Extended warranties and gadget insurance often have high margins for the seller. The expected payout is much lower than the premium.
Self-insure

steps: Put the premiums into an emergency fund

deep.x: Priorities

items: Life if others depend on you

deep.x: Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience.

cards.title: Primes et franchises
cards.text: La prime est ce que vous payez régulièrement. La franchise (franquia) est ce que vous payez avant que l'assurance intervienne. Une franchise plus élevée signifie en général une prime plus basse.

deep.x: The premium is what you pay for cover. The deductible, franquia in Portugal, is the part of each claim you pay yourself. Choosing a higher deductible usually lowers the premium.
Example
If you rarely claim, policy B saves €100 a year.
Choosing

x: Pick a deductible you could pay comfortably from savings
Higher deductibles suit people with emergency funds
Consider how often you've claimed in the past

deep.x: Other terms
Use your emergency fund to self-insure small losses and pay less for insurance.

cards.title: Assurances obligatoires

items: Crédit immo. : vie et multirisque en général exigées

cards.text: Au Portugal, l'assurance responsabilité civile automobile est obligatoire. L'assurance incendie est exigée pour les immeubles en copropriété, et les banques l'imposent avec un crédit immobilier.

deep.x: Some insurance is required by law in Portugal, because uninsured losses would hurt others.
Car insurance

Third-party liability insurance is compulsory for every vehicle in circulation. If an uninsured driver causes damage, Portugal's Motor Guarantee Fund (Fundo de Garantia Automóvel) pays victims and then pursues the driver.
Buildings
For buildings under horizontal property (flats in a condominium), fire insurance is mandatory for both individual units and common parts.
Mortgages

items.b: choose another insurer with equivalent cover

deep.x: Employers
Employers must insure workers against workplace accidents.
You can usually move your mortgage-linked life insurance to a cheaper provider; the bank can't refuse an equivalent policy.

cards.title: Assurance vie
cards.text: L'assurance vie indemnise les proches à charge en cas de décès. Elle compte surtout quand d'autres dépendent de votre revenu, comme des enfants ou un conjoint avec un crédit immobilier commun.

deep.x: Life insurance pays a sum to your beneficiaries if you die. It matters most when others rely on your income.
Types
Who needs it
How much
A common starting point: enough to clear debts plus several years of income for dependants. Some advisers suggest about ten times annual income for young families.
When you may not

x: Single, no dependants, no debts
Enough savings to cover your family's needs

deep.x: Life insurance isn't for you; it's for the people who depend on you.

cards.title: Assurance santé
cards.text: Le SNS portugais assure les soins de santé publics. Une assurance santé privée peut réduire les délais de consultation, mais vérifiez les exclusions, les plafonds et les délais de carence.

deep.x: Portugal's National Health Service (SNS) provides universal public healthcare. Private health insurance mainly offers faster access to consultations and private hospitals.
Popularity
Several million people in Portugal have private health insurance, often through employers, mainly to shorten waits for specialist appointments and exams.
What to check
Health plans vs insurance

items.b: reimburses or pays covered costs up to limits
discounts at a network, not insurance

deep.x: Older age
Many policies raise prices sharply or stop renewing at older ages, just when health needs grow. Check renewal rules.
Know whether you're buying real insurance or just a discount card.

cards.title: Lisez les exclusions
cards.text: Ce qui n'est pas couvert compte autant que ce qui l'est. Inondations, tremblements de terre et maladies préexistantes sont des exclusions fréquentes.

deep.x: What a policy doesn't cover matters as much as what it does. Exclusions are where most claim disputes start.
Common surprises

x: Water damage from gradual leaks excluded, only sudden bursts covered
Valuables above a limit need separate listing
Home left empty for over a set number of days voids cover
Travel insurance excludes extreme sports

deep.x: Underinsurance

x: Home worth €200,000 insured for €100,000
Damage of €50,000
Payout may be only €25,000 (proportional rule)

deep.x: How to read a policy

steps: Ask about unclear points in writing

deep.x: If it's not in the policy, assume it's not covered.

cards.title: Aléa moral
cards.text: Une fois assurées, les personnes peuvent prendre plus de risques, sachant que quelqu'un d'autre paie. Franchises et quotes-parts aident à contrer cela.

deep.x: Moral hazard arises when people take more risks because someone else bears the cost. The term originated in insurance.
Examples
Countermeasures

items.b: you share the first part of losses
you pay a share of each cost

deep.x: Adverse selection
A related problem: people who know they're higher risk are more likely to buy insurance, so insurers ask questions and set prices by risk.
The 2008 financial crisis renewed debate about moral hazard: banks considered "too big to fail" may take excessive risks.

cards.title: Couverture sismique

items.w: « Mon assurance habitation couvre les séismes »
items.r: À vérifier : c'est souvent une option

cards.text: Vu l'histoire de 1755, la couverture tremblement de terre au Portugal est facultative et souvent exclue des contrats habitation standard. Beaucoup de logements ne sont pas assurés contre ce risque.

deep.x: Portugal sits near active fault lines, and the 1755 earthquake devastated Lisbon. Yet earthquake cover is optional and often excluded from standard home policies.

items.w: "My home insurance covers earthquakes"
items.r: Check: seismic cover is usually an optional extra

deep.x: The protection gap
Only a minority of Portuguese homes are estimated to have earthquake cover, so a major quake would leave most losses uninsured. Proposals for a national seismic fund have been discussed for years.
Cost

items.b: varies by region and building age
often a percentage of insured value

deep.x: Why it matters
Reducing risk

x: Check your policy for seismic cover
Know the building's age and structural condition
Consider the deductible: often 5% of the insured value

deep.x: In seismic regions, earthquake cover may be the most important clause in your home policy.

cards.title: Faire jouer la concurrence
cards.text: Comparez les contrats par garanties, exclusions et franchise, pas seulement par prime. Révisez chaque année ; la fidélité est rarement récompensée.

deep.x: Insurance prices for the same cover vary widely, and loyalty is rarely rewarded. Comparing every year can save a lot.
Price walking
Insurers have sometimes offered better prices to new customers than to loyal ones. The UK banned this "price walking" for home and car insurance in 2022.
How to compare
Regulator
In Portugal, the ASF (Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões) supervises insurers and handles complaints.
Bundles

items: may get better cover for each

deep.x: Spend an hour a year comparing; it often pays better than any other hour.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce qu'une franchise (franquia) ?
options: Ce que vous payez avant que l'assurance couvre le reste
quiz.explain: Franchise plus haute, prime plus basse.

quiz.q: Quelle assurance auto est obligatoire au Portugal ?
quiz.explain: Couvre les dommages causés aux tiers.

cards.title: Le piège de l'urgence
cards.text: La plupart des arnaques créent de l'urgence : « votre compte va être bloqué », « agissez maintenant ». La pression empêche de réfléchir. Les vraies banques ne vous pressent pas ainsi.

deep.x: Almost every scam uses urgency. Pressure stops you thinking, checking or asking someone. Legitimate organisations rarely demand instant action.

steps: You click, pay or share codes

deep.x: Typical lines
Why it works
Stress narrows attention and reduces careful reasoning. Scammers exploit fear (losing money), greed (a bargain) and love (a family member in trouble).
Your defence

x: Pause: no real emergency is solved in 60 seconds
Contact the organisation through its official number or app
Talk to someone you trust

items.w: Click the link in the urgent SMS
items.r: Close it, open the official app or call the number on your card

deep.x: Urgency is the scammer's best tool; slowing down is yours.

cards.title: Hameçonnage
cards.text: De faux e-mails, SMS ou appels se font passer pour votre banque, le fisc ou un transporteur, et vous demandent de cliquer sur un lien ou de communiquer des codes.

deep.x: Phishing uses fake emails, SMS (smishing) or calls (vishing) that pretend to come from trusted organisations, to steal passwords, card details or codes.
Spotting it

items.b: odd email address or unknown number

deep.x: Spoofing
Scammers can make calls and SMS appear to come from real numbers, even your bank's. A familiar sender name doesn't prove anything.
Safe habits

x: Never click links in unexpected messages
Type addresses yourself or use official apps
Enable two-factor authentication
Report phishing to the organisation being impersonated

deep.x: Portuguese scams often impersonate CTT (post), the Tax Authority, Segurança Social, EDP and banks.

cards.title: Ne partagez jamais vos codes

items.w: « La banque m'a appelé pour avoir mon code »
items.r: Raccrochez, appelez le numéro officiel

cards.text: Aucune vraie banque ne vous demandera le code PIN complet de votre carte, votre mot de passe bancaire en ligne ou le code à usage unique envoyé sur votre téléphone. Quiconque le demande est un escroc.

deep.x: Your PIN, online banking password and one-time codes are the keys to your money. No legitimate bank or authority will ever ask for them.

items.w: "The bank's security team needs the code we just sent you"
items.r: That's always a scam: hang up

deep.x: Why codes matter
One-time codes (OTP) authorise payments or new devices. Sharing one lets the scammer approve a transfer or link your account to their phone.
The fake bank call

steps: They know some of your details

deep.x: Your rights
Under EU payment rules, banks must refund unauthorised transactions unless you acted fraudulently or with gross negligence. Sharing codes may count as gross negligence, so prevention matters.

items: Never install remote-access apps on request

deep.x: If anyone asks for your code, the answer is always no.

cards.title: Arnaques « Salut papa, salut maman »
cards.text: Des escrocs écrivent à des parents en se faisant passer pour leur enfant avec un nouveau numéro, et demandent de l'argent d'urgence. Appelez l'ancien numéro de l'enfant pour vérifier.

deep.x: In this scam, widespread in Portugal, messages from an unknown number claim to be from a son or daughter who "lost their phone" and urgently needs money.

steps: "Olá mãe, this is my new number"
Asks for transfer or MB WAY

deep.x: Why it works

x: Parents want to help their children quickly
Messages are casual and believable
Excuses explain why they can't call

deep.x: How to check

items: Ask a question only they'd know

deep.x: Family code word
Some families agree a code word for emergencies. A scammer won't know it.

deep.w: A WhatsApp message with my child's photo is proof
deep.r: photos are easily copied from social media

deep.x: Verify through a separate channel before sending any money.

cards.title: Arnaques à l'investissement
cards.text: De fausses plateformes affichent des rendements impressionnants et vous laissent retirer de petites sommes pour gagner votre confiance, puis disparaissent avec les dépôts plus importants. Consultez les listes d'alertes des régulateurs.

deep.x: Investment scams use fake platforms that show impressive returns, often letting you withdraw small amounts to build trust, before blocking withdrawals of larger sums.
Warning signs
Recovery scams
After losing money, victims are often contacted by "recovery services" promising to get it back, for a fee. These are usually the same scammers again.
Ponzi schemes

items: returns paid from new investors' money

deep.x: Portugal's "Dona Branca" ran a notorious scheme in the 1980s, promising 10% monthly returns.
If you can't withdraw your money freely, it isn't an investment; it's a trap.

cards.title: Vérifiez le régulateur
cards.text: Au Portugal, la CMVM, la Banque du Portugal et l'ASF publient des listes d'entités non autorisées. Si une société n'est pas enregistrée, n'investissez pas.

deep.x: Before investing or borrowing, check that the company is authorised. Portuguese regulators publish registers and warnings about unauthorised entities.

items.b: securities, investment firms, crypto under MiCA

deep.x: How to check

steps: Confirm website and contact details match

deep.x: Clone firms
Scammers copy the names and details of genuine authorised firms. Contact the firm through details on the regulator's register, not the website you were sent.
Across Europe

x: Firms authorised in other EU countries may operate via "passporting"
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) links national warnings

deep.x: If it isn't on the register, don't send money.

cards.title: Arnaques sentimentales
cards.text: Les escrocs construisent pendant des semaines une relation en ligne, puis inventent des urgences ou des « opportunités » d'investissement. N'envoyez jamais d'argent à quelqu'un que vous n'avez jamais rencontré.

deep.x: Romance scammers build online relationships over weeks or months, then invent emergencies or investment opportunities. Victims lose money and suffer emotional harm.

steps: Contact on dating app or social media

deep.x: Red flags
Pig butchering
Combines romance and investment: the "partner" introduces a crypto trading platform that shows fake profits.
Protecting relatives
Older and isolated people are frequent targets. Talk openly with family about these scams without judgement.
Never send money to someone you haven't met in person.

cards.title: Sécurité de la carte
cards.text: Utilisez le sans contact et les notifications de l'appli, fixez des plafonds de dépenses et utilisez des cartes virtuelles pour les achats en ligne. Signalez immédiatement une carte perdue.

deep.x: Cards are convenient and well protected, if you use the security features available.
Practical tips

x: Turn on instant notifications for every payment
Use virtual or single-use cards for online shopping
Set limits for online and abroad spending
Cover the keypad when entering your PIN

deep.x: Strong customer authentication
EU rules (PSD2) require two-factor authentication for most online card payments, such as approval in your banking app plus a PIN or fingerprint.
Lost card

steps: Freeze in app or call bank

deep.x: Under EU rules, your liability for unauthorised payments with a lost or stolen card before reporting is limited to €50, unless you were grossly negligent.
Notifications turn fraud from a monthly surprise into an instant alert.

cards.title: Arnaques MB WAY

items.w: « Allez au distributeur pour recevoir le paiement »
items.r: Recevoir de l'argent n'exige jamais d'agir à un distributeur

cards.text: Des escrocs se faisant passer pour des acheteurs sur des places de marché vous demandent de « recevoir » de l'argent via MB WAY, mais vous guident en réalité pour l'envoyer ou lier leur téléphone à votre compte.

deep.x: A common Portuguese scam targets people selling items on online marketplaces. The "buyer" asks to pay with MB WAY, then guides the seller through steps that actually send money or link the scammer's phone to the seller's account.

items.w: "Go to an ATM and follow my steps to receive the payment"
items.r: You never need an ATM or code to receive MB WAY money

deep.x: How it works
Rules

items: Never go to an ATM for a buyer

deep.x: Verification of payee
Since October 2025, EU banks must check that the name of the recipient matches the account before you send a transfer, warning you of mismatches.
Receiving money never requires you to do anything at an ATM.

cards.title: Si cela arrive
cards.text: Contactez immédiatement votre banque pour bloquer cartes et virements, changez vos mots de passe, portez plainte et gardez les preuves. La rapidité améliore les chances de récupération.

deep.x: If you've been scammed, act fast. Speed increases the chance of stopping payments and limiting damage.

steps: Call bank to block cards and transfers

deep.x: Immediately

x: Call your bank's 24-hour line to block cards and accounts
Ask the bank to try to recall transfers
Change passwords, starting with email and banking
Remove any remote-access apps installed on request

deep.x: Report

items.b: report the fake profile or ad

deep.x: Keep evidence
Don't feel ashamed
Scams are designed by professionals to fool smart people. Reporting helps police and protects others.
Scammers often target past victims again with "recovery" offers; be sceptical of anyone promising to get your money back for a fee.

quiz.q: Une vraie banque vous demandera-t-elle votre code SMS à usage unique ?
quiz.explain: Raccrochez et appelez le numéro officiel.

quiz.q: Où vérifier si une société d'investissement est agréée au Portugal ?
options: Les listes de la CMVM et de la Banque du Portugal
Le site de la société elle-même
quiz.explain: Les régulateurs publient des alertes.

cards.title: Pourquoi les entreprises se cotent
cards.text: Les entreprises vendent des actions en Bourse pour lever des fonds de croissance. Les premiers investisseurs peuvent aussi vendre leurs parts. Se coter pour la première fois s'appelle une introduction en Bourse (IPO).

deep.x: A company "goes public" by selling shares on a stock exchange for the first time, in an initial public offering (IPO). It raises money from many investors and gives existing owners a way to sell.
Benefits

items: Liquidity for founders and early investors
Shares to pay staff or buy companies

deep.x: Costs

x: Fees for banks, lawyers and auditors
Ongoing reporting and disclosure rules
Pressure from quarterly results
Loss of some control

deep.x: Staying private

items: funding from private equity or venture capital

deep.x: Many fast-growing tech firms now stay private longer, raising large sums from private investors.
The Amsterdam Stock Exchange, founded in the early 1600s to trade shares of the Dutch East India Company, is often called the world's first modern stock exchange.

cards.title: Les Bourses

items.b: 50 grandes firmes de la zone euro

cards.text: Les Bourses sont des places de marché qui mettent en relation acheteurs et vendeurs. Celle du Portugal est Euronext Lisbonne ; son indice principal, le PSI, suit les plus grandes sociétés cotées.

deep.x: A stock exchange is a regulated marketplace where buyers and sellers trade shares, bonds and funds. Electronic order books match orders in milliseconds.

items.b: Portugal's exchange, part of pan-European Euronext

deep.x: Euronext
Euronext operates exchanges including Amsterdam, Brussels, Dublin, Lisbon, Milan, Oslo and Paris, forming one of Europe's largest markets.
The PSI
The PSI (formerly PSI-20) tracks the largest and most traded Portuguese companies. Since 2022 its number of members can vary.
How a trade works

steps: You place an order with a broker

deep.x: Portugal's market is small; most investors also invest abroad for diversification.

cards.title: Ce qui fait bouger les prix
cards.text: Les prix bougent selon l'offre et la demande, sous l'effet des profits futurs attendus, des taux d'intérêt, de l'actualité et du sentiment.

deep.x: Share prices reflect what buyers and sellers think a company's future profits are worth. Expectations, not just results, move prices.
Expectations matter
A company can report record profits and see its share price fall, if investors expected even more.

items: price often falls, even if profits grew

deep.x: Interest rates
Short term vs long term
Benjamin Graham said the market is a voting machine in the short run and a weighing machine in the long run.

x: Short term: news, sentiment and flows dominate
Long term: profits and dividends drive returns

deep.x: Prices move on surprises: what's already expected is already in the price.

cards.title: Indices
cards.text: Un indice suit un panier d'actions pour montrer comment se porte un marché. Le S&P 500 comprend environ 500 des plus grandes entreprises américaines, pondérées selon leur taille.

deep.x: A stock market index tracks a basket of shares to measure how a market or segment performs. Many funds are built to copy indices.

items.b: about 500 large US companies, weighted by size

deep.x: Weighting
Concentration
In market-cap indices, the largest companies can dominate. By 2024–25, a handful of US tech giants made up roughly a third of the S&P 500's value.
Price vs total return

x: Price index: only price changes
Total return index: includes reinvested dividends, a fairer measure of investor returns

deep.x: An index is a shortcut to owning a market without picking winners.

cards.title: Marchés haussiers et baissiers
cards.text: Un marché haussier (bull) est une hausse soutenue ; un marché baissier (bear) est une chute de 20 % ou plus depuis un sommet. Le taureau charge vers le haut ; l'ours frappe vers le bas.

deep.x: Markets alternate between long rises (bull markets) and sharp falls (bear markets), commonly defined as declines of 20% or more from a peak.
Recent bear markets
Corrections
A fall of 10–20% is usually called a correction. They happen often, roughly every year or two on average.
Where the names come from
A bull attacks by thrusting its horns up; a bear swipes its paws down.
Historically, US bull markets have lasted several years on average, while bear markets have typically lasted around a year.

cards.title: Rendements à long terme

viz.unit: rendement réel % par an (long terme, approx.)

cards.text: Sur de longues périodes, les actions mondiales ont rapporté en moyenne environ 5 % par an au-dessus de l'inflation, mais avec de fortes fluctuations et de longues périodes sans progression.

deep.x: Over long periods, shares have delivered higher returns than bonds or cash, but with large swings along the way.
The source
These estimates come from the long-running research of Elroy Dimson, Paul Marsh and Mike Staunton, published annually in the UBS Global Investment Returns Yearbook.
Compounding the difference

x: 5% real a year for 30 years
= buying power multiplied by about 4.3
vs 1.3 for cash at 1%

deep.x: Long flat periods

x: Japanese shares took over 30 years to regain their 1989 peak
US shares went sideways in real terms from the mid-1960s to early 1980s
Diversifying across countries reduces this risk

deep.x: Shares reward patience, but not on a schedule.

cards.title: Baisses maximales
cards.text: Même les bons marchés subissent de grosses chutes. Les actions mondiales ont perdu environ 50 % en 2008-2009 et autour de 34 % en quelques semaines début 2020, avant de se redresser.

deep.x: A drawdown is the fall from a peak to a trough. Even excellent long-term investments go through deep drawdowns.
Recovery times

items.b: about four to five years to recover

deep.x: Why they matter

x: The temptation to sell at the bottom is strongest
Money needed soon shouldn't be in shares
Investing regularly buys more shares when prices are low

deep.x: Preparing
If you can't stomach a 50% fall, hold fewer shares.

cards.title: ETF
cards.text: Les fonds négociés en Bourse (ETF) détiennent des paniers d'actifs et s'échangent comme des actions. Un seul ETF monde peut vous donner des milliers d'entreprises à faible coût.

deep.x: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) hold baskets of assets and trade on exchanges like shares. They make broad diversification cheap and simple.
What one ETF can hold
A single world equity ETF can own shares in over a thousand companies across dozens of countries.
Types
Accumulating vs distributing
Things to check

x: Total expense ratio (TER)
Index tracked
Fund size and liquidity
Domicile, which affects taxes on dividends

deep.x: The first US ETF, tracking the S&P 500, launched in 1993 and is still one of the most traded securities in the world.

cards.title: Coûts
cards.text: Frais de fonds (TER), commissions de courtage, conversion de devises et impôts rognent tous les rendements. Sur des décennies, de petites différences se cumulent.

deep.x: Investment costs compound over time, just like returns. Small differences in fees can mean large differences after decades.
The effect of fees
Typical costs
Hidden costs

x: Currency conversion spreads when buying foreign shares
Custody fees charged by some banks
Frequent trading costs

deep.x: You can't control markets, but you can control costs.

cards.title: Impôt sur les plus-values au Portugal
cards.text: Les gains de cession d'actions et les dividendes sont en général imposés à un taux forfaitaire de 28 % au Portugal, avec la possibilité de les intégrer à l'impôt sur le revenu. Les règles changent ; vérifiez la loi en vigueur.

deep.x: In Portugal, gains from selling shares and dividends received are generally taxed at a flat 28%. Residents can choose to add this income to their other income instead ("englobamento").
Choosing englobamento
Short-term gains
Since 2023, gains on assets held for less than a year must be added to other income if your taxable income is in the top bracket.
Losses
Losses can offset gains in the same year, and if you choose englobamento, can be carried forward for several years.
Foreign investments
Tax rules change frequently; check the Portal das Finanças or an adviser before acting.

quiz.q: Qu'est-ce qu'un marché baissier (bear market) ?

quiz.explain: Le taureau charge vers le haut ; l'ours frappe vers le bas.

quiz.q: Que propose un ETF ?
options: Un panier d'actifs négocié comme une action
quiz.explain: De la diversification à faible coût.
